text:
The US Army is set to detonate the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning, moving ahead after multiple delays and despite an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.
The controlled blast is planned to dispose of 9,700lb (4,400kg) of the bomb-making chemicals stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa that is home to about 400 people. The explosion risks releasing plumes of toxic chemicals in a 100-mile (160km) radius, but exactly where those toxins will land has changed as the weather forecast changes.
On Tuesday, the army released new maps forecasting that the projected path will move south-west of Middletown before extending into northern Missouri.
The army has warned that “All people, but especially infants, children, pregnant women, adults and children with chronic diseases such as heart disease, kidney disease, or dementia, should avoid outdoor activities within affected areas until further guidance is provided”
The detonation is currently scheduled for 10am ET. In a public safety advisory released on Tuesday, the army said: “A more precise time will be communicated after evaluating changing weather patterns and waiting for the safest possible conditions.”
At a press conference on Tuesday, officials said they were not able to find a “viable alternative” after the material was discovered to be dangerously unstable earlier this year.
“There is consensus across experts across the country that a controlled, mitigated detonation of the lead azide here at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is far preferable to an uncontrolled, spontaneous detonation of that substance,” said Adam Telle, acting secretary of the US Army.
In a statement on Tuesday, senator-elect Josh Turek said he had been briefed on the detonation, adding that the chemicals “should never have been allowed to degrade to this point”.
“I will continue asking questions about how we got here. There is no excuse for such a failure of transparency and communication, especially when the health and safety of the public is involved,” he said.
The Federal Emergency Management Agency (Fema) is supporting “relocation for all residents of Middletown, Iowa, and immediate surrounding impacted areas”, according to the army, “out of an abundance of caution”.
In a social media post, homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said: “FEMA will ensure every resident who needs to temporarily evacuate will receive the support they need, including transportation, lodging, meals and other essential assistance.”
“We’ve made it very clear to those who are within a southwesterly location: if they choose to relocate, we will offer services,” Fema administrator Cameron Hamilton said in a statement.
On Tuesday, Iowa governor Kim Reynolds issued a proclamation of disaster emergency for Des Moines, Lee and Van Buren counties. With Reynolds’s approval, the Iowa national guard is providing up to 100 federally activated soldiers to support public safety and community outreach efforts around the detonation.
“Iowa agencies are actively engaged alongside our federal and local partners, and we remain focused on ensuring communities have the information and resources they need before, during, and after the operation,” Reynolds said in a statement.
An emergency notification sent to cellphones on Tuesday said that some people within five miles south-west of the plant may be evacuated and warned those up to 20 miles away to remain indoors with windows closed to “avoid airborne lead dust, noise and vibration”. The army encouraged residents who live outside the recommended evacuation zone to shelter in place.
The operation was initially planned for last Friday, but was rescheduled three times as public concern grew and environmentalists sued to block the detonation.
Donald Trump ordered the military to hold off on detonation pending a court ruling and a sign-off from the Democratic governor-elect, Rob Sand, who does not take office until January.
On Monday, a three-judge panel of the eighth circuit court of appeals said the army could proceed with detonating the stockpile, finding that the Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards in an emergency permit to minimize the dispersal of dust.
digest_he:
הצבא האמריקאי נערך לבצע פיצוץ מבוקר של מאגר חומרי הנפץ מסוג עופרת אזיד במפעל החימוש באיווה. המבצע יוצא לדרך לאחר עיכובים רבים וחששות ציבוריים כבדים מפני השפעות בריאותיות וסביבתיות, ובשל חוסר יציבות מסוכן שזוהה בחומרי המאגר המכילים אלפי קילוגרמים של כימיקלים.

הרשויות בארצות הברית פרסמו התזהרות והנחיות לתושבי האזור להישאר בבתים או להתפנות מתוך משנה זהירות, עקב החשש מפני שחרור עננים רעילים ואבק עופרת באוויר בהתאם לשינויי מזג האוויר. מושלת איווה הכריזה על מצב חירום באזורים הסמוכים, ומשמר הלאומי הופעל כדי לסייע במאמצי הבטיחות וההגנה על הציבור טרם ביצוע הפעולה.
